evidence.statement: Reachability is a real constraint on this ICP, not an accident of one bad list. Of 12 UK MSP contact pages checked on 2026-08-20, 5 published a usable commercial address, 3 obfuscated it behind Cloudflare, 2 published only a support address, and 2 published none at all. Three of the four EXP-ACQ-0001 bounces were the company's own published route rejecting or hiding external email.

A published, non-obfuscated, non-support address is NOT sufficient for reachability. AMVIA's hello@amvia.co.uk was verified on their own contact page on 2026-08-20 and hard-bounced 'address not found' six seconds after sending. 1 of 5 replacements failed on a criterion designed to prevent exactly that. Publication proves intent, not that the mailbox exists; only a send proves delivery.

EXP-CREATIVE-0001 could not be preregistered on 2026-08-21: no baseline exists for contact_intent, so success and review thresholds could only have been invented. Power analysis shows 870 sessions across both arms in the most generous case (5% baseline doubling) and 15,500 in the least (1% to 1.5%). Outbound is the only channel with real exposure and is occupied by EXP-ACQ-0001; every other channel is not_started. The constraint is audience, not experiment machinery.
evidence.source: power analysis + channels registry + empty experiment_trust_results, 2026-08-21

evidence.statement: EXP-ACQ-0001 reached its 50-send minimum and recorded REVIEW on 2026-08-27: 50 counted sends (55 rows, 5 bounces excluded), 0 meaningful replies, observed 0.0 against a 0.10 KEEP and 0.05 REVIEW threshold. evidence.statement: EXP-ACQ-0002 preregistered 2026-08-27 to test the route EXP-ACQ-0001 never tested: the same message delivered to a named buyer's own mailbox. KEEP >=10%, ITERATE 5-9.9%, REVIEW <5% (unchanged, so the two routes stay comparable), minimum sample 30 delivered named_buyer sends. n=30 rejects KEEP if it returns zero (P=4.2% at a true 10%) but cannot reject ITERATE (P=21.5% at a true 5%); roughly 60 would be needed for that. Contact discovery is an admission gate, not a step. Zero sends executed: outreach is external surface and is proposed, not run unattended.

Contact discovery for EXP-ACQ-0002 found 0 reachable named-buyer mailboxes across 18 observed UK MSP accounts (Wilson 95% CI 0-17.6%, implying a ceiling of ~10 across all 55). Reaching the 30-send minimum would require a 54.5% publication rate; P(observing 0 in 18 at that rate) = 7e-7. EXP-ACQ-0001 independently found 2 personal addresses across 27 named accounts (7.4%, upper bound 23.4% = 13 accounts). Named decision-makers were found for essentially every account with public LinkedIn profiles: the constraint is the mailbox, not the person. Mid-market UK MSPs do not publish commercial decision-makers' addresses, so for this ICP cold email is structurally a shared-inbox channel - already measured at 0/48. EXP-ACQ-0002 does not start; its contract was not relaxed to fit the supply.

Every apparent named-buyer address in the discovery run came from an enrichment aggregator and none survived first-party verification. pjob@intergence.com was reported by a search summariser as listed in Intergence's official contact details; the contact page carries only contact@, support@ and itsupport@, and the leadership page names six people and publishes no address. Others were masked (m*****@zenzero.co.uk, l******@ramsac.com), inferred from a stated format, or mutually inconsistent (three different addresses for Wavex's CEO). An inferred address is a hypothesis about a mail server, which is where four of EXP-ACQ-0001's five lost sends died.
evidence.source: WebFetch of intergence.com/contact and /why-intergence versus search summaries, 2026-08-27

evidence.statement: LinkedIn Help states verbatim: 'Basic and free LinkedIn members can include a personalized message to five connection requests per month. LinkedIn Premium members can send unlimited personalized messages with their connection requests.' Five per month makes a 30-send minimum take six months on a free account, so the LinkedIn route cannot be run unpaid. LinkedIn does not publish its invitation thresholds ('LinkedIn Support cannot disclose the type or reason for the restriction'); the widely-quoted weekly caps and note character limits come from automation vendors selling tools to exceed them and are recorded as unverified.

LinkedIn's own compare-plans page lists Sales Navigator Core at US$119.99/month (US$1,079.88/year) and Advanced at US$159.99/month (US$1,799.88/year), both with 50 InMail credits per month. GBP figures appear on the page but were not captured; a widely-quoted GBP94.99 for Core is unverified. Sales Navigator is likely the wrong purchase: the binding constraint is personalised connection notes, which any Premium account unlocks, and Premium is cheaper. Sales Navigator's search filters and InMail credits are not needed when the account list already exists in sales/teardowns/.

The LinkedIn route is not metrically comparable to EXP-ACQ-0001. Email had one step (arrived or bounced); LinkedIn has invite -> accept -> message -> reply. A connection request is not a delivery: an unaccepted invite is never read and is not a bounce either, it is a silent non-event. Reusing the 10%/5% thresholds would compare two different quantities. The honest primary metric is a funnel with invite-accept rate as the new unknown, which has no baseline. The note is also character-limited, so the OBSERVATION + ECONOMIC HYPOTHESIS + CTA message cannot be sent as written - the channel change forces a message change, and that confound must be designed around before running, not explained afterwards.

Owned-site traffic, read from Vercel's Web Analytics API via the authenticated CLI. Analytics was enabled 2026-08-20 11:25 BST; there is no earlier data. Daily visitors/pageviews: 08-20 15/26, 08-21 9/10, 08-22 6/9, 08-23 0/0, 08-24 2/2, 08-25 2/2, 08-26 0/0, 08-27 0/0, 08-28 1/1. All time 35 visitors / 50 pageviews; clean window from 2026-08-22 is 11 visitors / 14 pageviews in seven days - about 1.6 visitors a day or 47 a month. Referrers: a single empty-hostname row covering all 35 visitors, so no channel is referring anyone. Paths: / 34 visitors, /insights 1, /privacy 1. Note the endpoint silently ignores from/to and only honours since/until, so the echoed query window must be read rather than the requested one.

The conversion numerator is paywalled. /v1/query/web-analytics/events/count returns 'Accessing Analytics custom events requires an Enterprise or Pro plan. (402)' and the team billing plan is 'hobby'. contact_intent is a custom event, so it cannot be counted now or in future without upgrading. The baseline window therefore could never have produced a rate: its denominator was 30x smaller than recorded and its numerator is unreadable.

EXP-CREATIVE-0001 is not runnable on theplus-tech.com and the constraint is audience, not creative. At 11 visitors a week the most generous cell in the preregistered power table (870 sessions across both arms, 5% to 10%) takes 1.5 years to fill; 1% to 1.5% takes 27 years. The baseline window was opened for four weeks on 2026-08-21 and closed after one because the reading is decisive. No creative experiment is preregistered. Combined with EXP-ACQ-0001 closing the shared-inbox route at 0/48 and EXP-ACQ-0002 finding the personal route unreachable, distribution is the constraint across every channel measured so far; nothing in the creative, offer or messaging layer has been falsified because none of it has been given a sample.

The unit is the post and the median is reported alongside the total, because LinkedIn supplies the distribution and one post that travels would otherwise define a baseline nothing reproduces. evidence.statement: The redesign shipped a favicon that was served but never referenced. public/favicon.svg and public/site.webmanifest both returned 200 from the day they were added while the rendered HTML carried no rel=icon and no rel=manifest, so every browser fell back to /favicon.ico, which 404s. A file in public/ is served, not linked - Next injects the tag only for app/icon.* or for what metadata declares. Found by fetching the deployed page and grepping it rather than by trusting the commit message that said 'favicon'. Fixed in 86654c5 and both link tags confirmed in the live HTML.
evidence.source: curl of https://theplus-tech.com plus .next build output, 2026-08-28

evidence.statement: A Vercel deploy reaching READY is not proof the apex serves it. Immediately after the favicon deploy went READY the apex returned the previous HTML with x-vercel-cache: HIT and age: 180, byte-identical to the pre-deploy copy, and a cache-busting query string did not change the cache key. The deployment URL itself 302s under deployment protection, so the origin check needs 'vercel curl', which returned the correct 20,145-byte page with both link tags. The apex caught up shortly after with x-vercel-cache: PRERENDER and age: 0. Ask the origin, not the edge - and re-check the edge before claiming a user can see it.
evidence.source: curl response headers against theplus-tech.com and vercel curl against the deployment URL, 2026-08-28

evidence.statement: The site sells two different products at one price. A buyer clicking 'Rescue Sprint 1500' on the homepage lands on /workflow-audit whose deliverables do not overlap with what the homepage promised: ten labels extracted from the DOM of both pages, five on each side, ZERO shared. Homepage: workflow and evidence-source map, reusable answer bank, missing-controls report, exportable response pack, 30-day automation roadmap. Landing page: workflow map, opportunity register, risk and compliance flags, ROI estimate, 30-day build roadmap. Naming is three-way inconsistent in the same click path - homepage H2 'Security Questionnaire Rescue Sprint', page title 'AI Workflow Opportunity Audit', page H1 'Find the workflow worth automating', body says 'audit', buttons say 'sprint'. Scored with the repo's own CongruenceScore: audience 4, problem 2, message 1, visual 5, offer 0, cta 4 = 16/30, DO_NOT_SPEND. visual 5 against offer 0 is the whole finding: it looks like one product and describes two. This independently confirms the channel screen's block on paid media by a different route. Which offer is real is a positioning decision and was deliberately not resolved here.
evidence.source: Playwright DOM extraction of theplus-tech.com and /workflow-audit + CongruenceScore, 2026-08-29

evidence.statement: Every call to action on the homepage and the paid-offer page resolves to mailto:ogievatheophilus@gmail.com, and the sprint page footer reads 'Confidential enquiries to ogievatheophilus@gmail.com'. The offer is evidence, compliance and security posture sold to regulated buyers, so the word confidential beside a personal Gmail address undercuts the argument before the page is read. The domain already runs Google Workspace (v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com on theplus-tech.com), so a domain mailbox is likely already available or one console action away - cheap to fix rather than a project.
evidence.source: Playwright mailto extraction + dig TXT theplus-tech.com, 2026-08-29

evidence.statement: Visual review of the shipped redesign in a real browser engine at 1440 and 390. scrollWidth - clientWidth = 0 on both the homepage and the sprint page at 390, single column, masthead wraps rather than toggling, evidence tables stay inside their containers. All checked routes 200 and /nope 404s; the only console error in the session was the reviewer's own probe of /nope. The review ran with ?internal=1, which tested the internal-traffic exclusion end to end for the first time: localStorage tpt_internal_traffic = '1' and console '[analytics] internal traffic exclusion: ON'. Typography at reading distance and colour on a calibrated display remain unreviewed - a rendering engine at two widths is not a person's eye.

The offer registry did not contain the company's own flagship. It held OFF-TEARDOWN, OFF-SPRINT, OFF-AI-COMPLIANCE and OFF-ARCH-ASSESSMENT while the live site's one purchasable offer - the GBP1,500 Security Questionnaire Rescue Sprint, marked binding twice in the website's PRODUCT.md - was absent. Added as OFF-RESCUE-SPRINT with 0 sends and 0 buyers.

The company markets two different problems to the same buyer. EXP-ACQ-0001's 50 sends pitched OFF-TEARDOWN: a free growth-leak teardown of the prospect's own site, problem 'acquisition not becoming qualified pipeline', laddering to a 30-Day Pipeline Engineering Sprint. The live site sells OFF-RESCUE-SPRINT at GBP1,500, problem 'trust answers rebuilt from scratch on every deal'. Both target founders and MDs of UK cyber firms and MSPs. Neither has a buyer. This is a strategy conflict rather than a copy defect and was deliberately not resolved: the outbound offer has measured non-response on the shared-inbox route (0/48) and the site offer has never been taken to market at all, so no evidence distinguishes them.

Offer congruence fixed and verified live 2026-08-29 (main@c030e5b). All five flagship deliverables now appear on BOTH theplus-tech.com and /workflow-audit - 5/5 shared where it was 0/10 - and the four old-offer labels (Opportunity register, ROI estimate, Risk and compliance flags, AI Workflow Opportunity Audit) return 0 occurrences on the live page. Page title is now 'Security Questionnaire Rescue Sprint'. CongruenceScore went 16/30 DO_NOT_SPEND to 29/30 ELIGIBLE_FOR_TEST; message_match is held at 4 rather than 5 because the URL is still /workflow-audit and a buyer sees it. Root cause was a duplicated offer definition, not positioning: site-data.ts already declared flagship as 'the one purchasable offer, price and framing binding' and the page imported it for the price while redefining the deliverables beside it. Fixed by making flagship the single source and guarding it with a binding-declaration test and a negative test, both observed failing first.
evidence.source: curl of both live pages + CongruenceScore, 2026-08-29

evidence.statement: The GrowthOps Command Center now executes a human-gated outbound lifecycle rather than only reporting state. A real-browser test against an isolated store created a sourced observation + economic hypothesis + low-friction CTA draft, persisted its teardown, approved it, recorded an operator-confirmed manual send, then recorded a meaningful reply. The scoreboard moved from 0/0 to one delivered and one reply; route integrity reported email/named_buyer 1/1. The production-shaped store exposed 51 selectable actionable prospects with disqualified rows excluded. Desktop and mobile had zero horizontal overflow and zero console errors. There is no autosend interface; suppression is checked at draft creation and immediately before a manual send can be recorded.
evidence.source: isolated browser lifecycle + command-center HTTP and workbench tests, 2026-08-29

evidence.statement: An isolated real-browser lifecycle recorded a cited intent event with observed fact separate from commercial interpretation, moved one eligible account into Today's 10 best buyers, routed the missing recipient identity to research, then changed the action to Prepare approval draft after an observed_published identity fixture was added. The prepared draft inherited the signal, source, fact, hypothesis, identity and channel; after creation both the draft and buyer card showed one linked outcome. Zero sends occurred. Deterministic tests cover hard disqualification, freshness, confidence, alternate eligible signals, identity provenance, private-network rejection and Signal to Draft to Reply lineage. The real operational store received schema only and contains no fabricated signal or identity rows.
evidence.source: isolated browser buyer-desk lifecycle + signal intelligence, HTTP and workbench tests, 2026-08-30
